name: Patient Health Questionnaire 2
construct: Ultra brief depression screen covering depressed mood and anhedonia over the past 2 weeks.
licence: "No permission required to reproduce, translate, display or distribute." Developed by Drs Spitzer, Williams and Kroenke and colleagues with an educational grant from Pfizer Inc.
instructions: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following problems?

items.text: Little interest or pleasure in doing things

scoring: Sum the 2 items for a total of 0 to 6; higher scores indicate more frequent depressive symptoms. Kroenke, Spitzer and Williams (2003) identify a cut off of 3 or more as the optimal positive screen; a cut point of 2 increases sensitivity. Positive screens should be followed with the PHQ-9 or clinical assessment. Source: NIDA CDE page and Kroenke et al. (2003).
citation: Kroenke, K., Spitzer, R. L., & Williams, J. B. W. (2003). The Patient Health Questionnaire-2: Validity of a two-item depression screener. Medical Care, 41(11), 1284-1292. https://doi.org/10.1097/01.MLR.0000093487.78664.3C
transcriptionNote: The phqscreeners.com home page (itemsUrl) and the NIDA CDE page (sourceUrl in the target) describe the measure but do not print the items, so the stem, the 2 items and the response options were transcribed from the PsyToolkit PHQ-9 page, where they appear as items 1 and 2 of the PHQ-9; the PHQ-2 consists of these 2 items unchanged. PsyToolkit prints the response labels in lower case; sentence case is used above as on the PHQ forms. The NIDA CDE page supplied the scoring, cut offs and permission statement.
